fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Fortune Card and the Turning Wheel", "body": "Chance said the Fortune card, the Wheel of Fortune in the Crowley deck, was the main card for the episode, and he noted that the camera turned a full 360 degrees right after the opening screen. He tied the Hebrew letter kaf, meaning palm or grasp, to the many hands, raised palms and the Sylvie grasping the smoke monster, using words from a gematria PDF a viewer shared. The hosts assigned Sphinx, Typhon and Hermanubis roles on the card to Sylvie, the smoke monster and the Lokis, and Gabe agreed the wheel recurred throughout."}, {"title": "Towers, Lighthouses and the Void", "body": "Chance followed the sight of the Lighthouse of Alexandria into a tangent on towers, stupas and the Greco-Buddhist world, and said the fog of time concealed earlier civilizations in the show. He read the void through letter swaps, arguing that vacus became Bacchus, and described purgatory as a place of temporary punishment. One of the hosts read Mobius as the chariot and tower and suggested that Loki mixed the Moon and Hanged Man cards. The hosts linked the smoke monster Alioth to Typhon and to a star in Ursa Major."}, {"title": "Sobek, Epithets and One Underlying Figure", "body": "Chance restated his theory that the ancient world's crowd of gods grew from titles and epithets mistaken for separate beings, and used Sobek as his example, saying Sobek, Horus and Osiris overlapped. He read the crocodile Loki as a sovereign and Jesus-like figure and read the void turkeys as peacocks tied to death and rebirth. Gabe added that Sobek sat under the boot on the Thoth Fool card, which he called the subconscious, and linked the peacocks to the Pavo constellation."}, {"title": "The Symposium Scene and the Official Timeline", "body": "Gabe argued that the bunker scene mirrored Plato's Symposium, with each Loki taking a turn speaking and the main Loki giving a eulogy about love that invoked Sophia, while the group laughed him down. He later described Dylan's chat point and his own work on the speakers and muses. One of the hosts said the Polybius arcade box also pointed to the historian Polybius, whom he called the father of the sacred timeline, and the hosts compared the game legend with the official story."}, {"title": "Ascending Through the Parts of Yourself", "body": "Chance closed by saying the episode introduced the show's largest theme, ascending to godhood by perfecting every part of yourself, and he compared purgatory and penance to resolving old patterns. The hosts read Ophiuchus as a gate out of the zodiac animals, and Chance traced the snakes versus wolves line to the Ophites. Gabe's closing remarks read the cleared smoke as the end of the air season and the move into an earth element, with the group crossing a symbolic solstice as the episode ended."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The fifth installment of our Loki series might be the most jam packed yet. Themes of purgatory, penance, the Wheel of Fortune, and the Void all revolve around this episode, along with more clues to the artificial history timeline. There's even a homunculus in this one! Tune in to find out what the many alternate Lokis and the giant smoke monster at the end of time represent in occultism.
